root_cause.text: In netfilter ctnetlink expectation creation, userspace could supply a CTA_EXPECT_HELP_NAME helper different from the master conntrack’s actual helper, so CTA_EXPECT_CLASS was validated and the expectation was built against mismatched helper metadata, leading to out-of-bounds access in nf_ct_expect_related_report.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes all userspace helper lookup/use from ctnetlink_glue_attach_expect() and ctnetlink_create_expect(), changes ctnetlink_alloc_expect() to always fetch `helper = rcu_dereference(help->helper)` from the master conntrack, and the CVE/commit message explicitly says the bug was triggered by “validating CTA_EXPECT_CLASS via different helper provided by userspace than the existing master conntrack helper,” causing a KASAN slab-out-of-bounds read.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In netfilter ctnetlink expectation creation, userspace could supply a CTA_EXPECT_HELP_NAME helper different from the master conntrack’s actual helper, so CTA_EXPECT_CLASS was validated and the expectation was built against mismatched helper metadata, leading to out-of-bounds access in nf_ct_expect_related_report.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes all userspace helper lookup/use from ctnetlink_glue_attach_expect() and ctnetlink_create_expect(), changes ctnetlink_alloc_expect() to always fetch `helper = rcu_dereference(help->helper)` from the master conntrack, and the CVE/commit message explicitly says the bug was triggered by “validating CTA_EXPECT_CLASS via different helper provided by userspace than the existing master conntrack helper,” causing a KASAN slab-out-of-bounds read.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused helper parameter from ctnetlink_alloc_expect to simplify its interface without changing intended behavior.
intent_record.what: The function declaration of ctnetlink_alloc_expect was changed to remove the struct nf_conntrack_helper *helper parameter, leaving only the cda array, nf_conn pointer, tuple pointer, and mask pointer arguments.
intent_record.how: At runtime this changes the function interface so callers and the implementation no longer pass or depend on a helper argument when allocating an expectation, indicating the helper input was unnecessary or is now obtained elsewhere rather than supplied directly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unused `helper` local variable from `ctnetlink_glue_attach_expect` as a cleanup with no functional change.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration `struct nf_conntrack_helper *helper = NULL;` was removed from `ctnetlink_glue_attach_expect`, leaving the other local declarations unchanged.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior directly; it removes an unused local variable, reducing dead code and avoiding an unnecessary declaration/initialization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove helper-name lookup and pass fewer arguments so expectation handling is delegated to ctnetlink_alloc_expect().
intent_record.what: The change removes the conditional block that read CTA_EXPECT_HELP_NAME from the parsed netlink attributes, extracted the helper name with nla_data(), looked up a conntrack helper via __nf_conntrack_helper_find(), and returned -EOPNOTSUPP if no helper was found; it also updates the ctnetlink_alloc_expect() call to no longer pass the helper argument, reducing its arguments from (attrs, ct, helper, &tuple, &mask) to (attrs, ct, &tuple, &mask).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this function no longer performs an explicit helper-name-based conntrack helper lookup before allocating the expectation, and it no longer fails early with -EOPNOTSUPP when the named helper is missing. Expectation allocation is now delegated without a helper parameter, implying helper selection or validation is handled elsewhere or no longer required at this call site.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor ctnetlink_alloc_expect() to stop taking the helper as an argument and use an internally managed helper variable instead.
intent_record.what: The function signature of ctnetlink_alloc_expect() was changed to remove the struct nf_conntrack_helper *helper parameter, and a new local declaration of struct nf_conntrack_helper *helper was added inside the function body after obtaining the net pointer.
intent_record.how: This makes helper no longer provided by the caller and instead prepared to be determined internally within ctnetlink_alloc_expect(), shifting helper sourcing into the function rather than passing it as an argument.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fetch and validate the conntrack helper before processing expectation class attributes to safely reject unsupported cases.
intent_record.what: The code now assigns `helper = rcu_dereference(help->helper);` after verifying `help` is non-NULL, adds a new `if (!helper) return ERR_PTR(-EOPNOTSUPP);` check, and changes the subsequent condition from `if (cda[CTA_EXPECT_CLASS] && helper)` to `if (cda[CTA_EXPECT_CLASS])`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this ensures the helper pointer is explicitly retrieved from `help->helper` under RCU protection and validated before any access to `helper->expect_class_max`. It prevents proceeding with expectation-class handling when no helper is attached, returning `-EOPNOTSUPP` earlier instead of risking invalid or inconsistent helper usage.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop implicitly inheriting the helper from `help->helper` when creating an expectation and use only the explicitly provided helper pointer.
intent_record.what: The conditional block that checked `if (!helper)` and assigned `helper = rcu_dereference(help->helper);` was removed, leaving only the existing `rcu_assign_pointer(exp->helper, helper);` assignment.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer falls back to reading `help->helper` when the local `helper` pointer is NULL, so `exp->helper` is assigned only the explicitly provided `helper` value, including NULL if none was supplied.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unused local helper pointer from ctnetlink_create_expect without changing behavior.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration `struct nf_conntrack_helper *helper = NULL;` was removed from `ctnetlink_create_expect`, while the surrounding declarations and function body context shown in the diff remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime this has no direct behavioral effect because it only eliminates an unused local pointer variable, reducing unnecessary stack/local state without changing execution logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Move conntrack helper handling out of ctnetlink_create_expect() by removing inline helper lookup/module-loading logic and simplifying expectation allocation.
intent_record.what: The change removes the entire block in ctnetlink_create_expect() that checked CTA_EXPECT_HELP_NAME, looked up a conntrack helper with __nf_conntrack_helper_find(), conditionally requested a helper module via request_module(), handled related error paths, and assigned a helper variable; it also changes the call to ctnetlink_alloc_expect() by removing the helper argument, from ctnetlink_alloc_expect(cda, ct, helper, &tuple, &mask) to ctnetlink_alloc_expect(cda, ct, &tuple, &mask).
intent_record.how: At runtime, ctnetlink_create_expect() no longer performs helper-name-based helper lookup or helper module autoloading before allocating an expectation. Expectation creation is now delegated to ctnetlink_alloc_expect() without passing a pre-resolved helper, which removes the old failure paths tied to missing helpers and centralizes or eliminates that behavior elsewhere.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unused error label from the conntrack expectation creation cleanup path without changing behavior.
intent_record.what: The unused error label `err_ct:` was removed from the error path, while the `nf_ct_put(ct);` call remains in place directly before the return after `rcu_read_unlock();`.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior because execution still unlocks RCU, decrements the conntrack reference with `nf_ct_put(ct)`, and returns the error value as before; it only removes an unnecessary jump label.

grouping_result.intent: Remove an unused error label from the conntrack expectation creation cleanup path without changing behavior.
Move conntrack helper handling out of ctnetlink_create_expect() by removing inline helper lookup/module-loading logic and simplifying expectation allocation.
Fetch and validate the conntrack helper before processing expectation class attributes to safely reject unsupported cases.
Stop implicitly inheriting the helper from `help->helper` when creating an expectation and use only the explicitly provided helper pointer.

consistency_review.core_intent: Clean up conntrack expectation creation code by removing unused helper-related variables/parameters and an unused cleanup label without changing behavior.
Refactor expectation creation so conntrack helper lookup and handling are moved out of ctnetlink_create_expect() and encapsulated within ctnetlink_alloc_expect().

relevance_review.reason: The changes are cleanup-only: removing unused helper variables/parameters and an unused label. They do not enforce matching CTA_EXPECT_HELP_NAME with the master conntrack helper, do not change CTA_EXPECT_CLASS validation, and do not affect expectation construction logic tied to the out-of-bounds root cause.

The vulnerability is caused by incorrect helper selection/validation during expectation creation. This group moves helper lookup and handling into ctnetlink_alloc_expect(), i.e. directly restructures the code path where the mismatched helper could be used, so it is tied to the root-cause logic rather than being a purely unrelated refactor.

The change directly addresses the root cause by obtaining and validating the actual conntrack helper before handling CTA_EXPECT_CLASS, preventing expectations from being created using mismatched helper metadata supplied from userspace.

The vulnerability is caused by creating expectations using helper metadata that can differ from the actual/validated helper. This change removes implicit inheritance from help->helper and relies only on the explicitly provided helper pointer, directly addressing the helper-mismatch condition behind the out-of-bounds access.

candidates.rationale: This gates CTA_EXPECT_CLASS validation on the userspace-supplied helper pointer rather than the master conntrack's actual helper, enabling validation against mismatched helper metadata.
This performs the class bounds check against the possibly attacker-chosen helper's expect_class_max, which is the core mismatch that can allow an invalid class for the real helper.
This conditional allows the code to keep using a non-NULL helper supplied from userspace instead of forcing use of the master conntrack's actual helper, permitting helper/class mismatch.
This stores the potentially mismatched helper into the expectation, so later code can operate on helper metadata inconsistent with the master conntrack state, leading to out-of-bounds access.

This looks up a helper purely by the userspace-provided CTA_EXPECT_HELP_NAME and passes it onward, creating the opportunity for an expectation to be validated and built against a helper different from the master conntrack's actual helper.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the entry point of the bug: it selects a helper based solely on the userspace-provided CTA_EXPECT_HELP_NAME, making it possible to use helper metadata that does not match the master conntrack's actual helper.
This validates CTA_EXPECT_CLASS against the attacker-selected helper's expect_class_max rather than the master conntrack's real helper, enabling acceptance of a class invalid for the real helper.

This installs the potentially mismatched helper into the expectation object, causing later expectation handling to use helper metadata inconsistent with the master conntrack and leading to out-of-bounds access.
This gates class validation on the presence of the userspace-selected helper, reinforcing the incorrect trust relationship and allowing CTA_EXPECT_CLASS processing against mismatched helper metadata.

This conditional preserves a non-NULL helper obtained from userspace instead of forcing use of the master conntrack's actual helper, enabling the helper/class mismatch to persist into expectation creation.
